identity.title: Discovery of a sub-Keplerian disk with jet around a 20 M<SUB>☉</SUB> young star. ALMA observations of G023.01-00.41

paper_type_evidence.quote: We observed the star-forming region G023.01$-$00.41 with the 12 m-array of ALMA in band 6 (211–275 GHz). Observations were conducted under program 2015.1.00615.S

evidence.quote: at a parallax distance of 4.6 kpc (cite: Brunthaler2009)

question.value: Is there a disk-jet system around the 20 Msun O-type young star in G023.01-00.41, and is the disk gas in centrifugal equilibrium (Keplerian) or infalling/sub-Keplerian?

evidence.quote: we seek to simultaneously resolve the spatial morphology of the disk and the regions where the jet originates, and to determine whether or not the disk gas is in centrifugal equilibrium.
Observations were conducted under program 2015.1.00615.S during two runs, on 2016 September 5 and 16 (Cycle 3)
with the 12 m-array of ALMA in band 6 (211–275 GHz)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 12 narrow spws of 234 MHz (960 channels, Hanning smoothed, 0.7 km/s) plus one 1875 MHz wide band (3840 channels, centered 217.860 GHz)

evidence.quote: to record 12 narrow spectral windows, each 234 MHz wide, and an additional wide band of 1875 MHz.
The wide band was correlated with 3840 channels and centered at a rest frequency of 217.860 GHz.
The 12 m-array observed with 45 antennas covering a baseline range between 16 m and 3143 m
covering a baseline range between 16 m and 3143 m
with the aim to achieve an angular resolution of $0.2\ensuremath{''}$
to recover extended emission over a maximum scale of $2''$

sensitivity.value: ~2 mJy/beam per narrow channel (1.4 K) expected; continuum S/N about 100

evidence.quote: thermal rms per (narrow) spectral channel of about 2 mJy beam$^{-1}$ (with 36 antennas)
We spent 1 hour of time on-source during a total observing time of 2 hours
on 2016 September 5 and 16 (Cycle 3)

evidence.quote: These values are calculated by Gaussian fitting the CH$_3$OH emission within the 60% contour level

evidence.quote: along a position angle of $-33^{\circ}$ on the sky plane (measured east of north)

validation.value: Star position chosen to maximize symmetry of blue and red sides

evidence.quote: The position of the central star was set as to maximize the symmetry of the blue- and redshifted sides of the disk

analysis_steps.goal: Build a radiative transfer disk model and compare pv-diagrams

method.value: Semi-analytic disk, RADMC-3D ray-tracing in LTE, observed with simobserve/simanalyze; pv-diagrams along the disk plane compared for infalling (70% free-fall) and Keplerian velocity fields

evidence.quote: the gas is moving radially at $70\%$ of the corresponding free-fall velocity

evidence.quote: We set a CH$_3$CN abundance relative to H$_2$ of $2\times10^{-8}$ at 500 au

evidence.quote: with a gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100 and a dust opacity of 1.0 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ at 1.3 mm

validation.value: Modeled peak dust and line brightness compared to observed

evidence.quote: the modeled peak brightness of both the CH$_3$CN line and the dust continuum coincides with the observed values.

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate disk mass from dust continuum

evidence.quote: We use an average gas temperature of 279 K, determined from the model between radii of 10 au and 2000 au

findings_qualitative.value: Disk gas is infalling near free-fall and sub-Keplerian outside ~500 au; Keplerian-like rotation possible only inside

evidence.quote: gas is falling in close to free-fall, and slowly rotating with sub-Keplerian velocities

findings_qualitative.value: A compact blueshifted molecular jet is detected from inner disk (<800 au); the redshifted lobe is not seen, interpreted as optically thick inner disk

evidence.quote: we do not detect the redshifted lobe of the jet

claims.hypothesis: A disk perpendicular to the outflow exists around the O-type YSO
claims.experiment: CH3OH moment maps and channel maps
claims.result: Flattened structure to ~2380 au with velocity gradient along major axis
claims.finding: A disk is present, warped in outer regions

evidence.quote: This piece of evidence satisfies the first condition, that of a highly flattened structure perpendicular to the outflow

claims.hypothesis: Disk gas is in centrifugal equilibrium
claims.experiment: Compare observed CH3CN pv-diagram with infalling and Keplerian RADMC-3D models
claims.result: Infall profile reproduces forbidden quadrants; Keplerian only needed at inner radii
claims.finding: Gas is infalling and sub-Keplerian outside ~500 au

evidence.quote: the condition of centrifugal equilibrium does not hold outside a radius of 500 au

claims.hypothesis: The disk mass is small relative to the star
claims.experiment: Dust continuum mass estimate and model
claims.result: 1.6 ± 0.3 Msun vs model 1.4 Msun at 2000 au
claims.finding: Disk mass ~10% of the stellar mass

evidence.quote: We conclude that very likely the disk mass is much less ($\sim$ 10%) than the mass of the star.

why_this_data.value: SMA data used to set requirements for higher-resolution ALMA observations

evidence.quote: to set up the requirements for higher resolution observations with ALMA

limitations_admitted.value: Inner regions sampled by only two beams; inner Keplerian possibility speculative

evidence.quote: the inner regions are sampled by only two beams with the current resolution

limitations_admitted.value: Model does not include envelope and uses simple power laws

evidence.quote: the model does not account for a dusty envelope surrounding the disk

referee_caveats_inferred: Model comparison is by eye with no quantitative fit or uncertainty on infall fraction
Stellar mass fixed from luminosity, so rotation/infall degeneracy not tested
Outflow contamination of CH3OH/CH3CN pv-diagrams complicates the interpretation
Disk mass depends on assumed opacity and temperature
